text:
# Kitchen Packing Plan

The idea is to pack in reverse order of need: things you won't touch until you're settled go in boxes first, and the stuff you need on day one stays out until the very end and travels with you or goes in a clearly labeled "OPEN FIRST" box.

---

## OPEN FIRST box (day-one essentials)

This box rides in the car or gets loaded last and unloaded first. Label it on all sides.

Coffee maker or pour-over and filters, coffee/tea. Two mugs, two plates, two bowls, two sets of utensils. A sharp knife, a cutting board, and a can opener. One small pot, one skillet. Dish soap, a sponge, and a dish towel. Paper towels and a roll of trash bags. A few zip-lock bags and aluminum foil. Snacks and anything shelf-stable you'll want that first night (peanut butter, crackers, granola bars). Dog bowls, a day's worth of dog food, and treats. Phone charger and a power strip if your kitchen is also your landing zone.

---

## PACK LAST (the week before)

These are things you're still using daily but can box up the morning of or the night before.

Remaining everyday dishes, glasses, and silverware. The toaster, kettle, or any small appliance you use every morning. Cooking utensils you're using right up to the end (spatula, wooden spoon, tongs). Spices and condiments you haven't tossed. Cleaning supplies for the final wipe-down. Remaining food — plan meals to use up what's in the fridge and freezer during the last week.

---

## PACK 2–3 WEEKS OUT

Bakeware (muffin tins, cookie sheets, cake pans). Specialty cookware (Dutch oven, wok, slow cooker, Instant Pot). Serving dishes, platters, and holiday items. Extra sets of dishes or glassware beyond your daily use. Vases, decorative items, and cookbook collection. Wine glasses, bar tools, and anything fragile you aren't using regularly. Small appliances you can live without (blender, food processor, stand mixer, waffle maker). Drawer clutter — junk drawer contents, rubber bands, twist ties, birthday candles.

---

## PACK FIRST (now-ish, 4+ weeks out)

Anything you forgot you owned. Tupperware lids with no matching container (toss them). Duplicate gadgets and unitaskers you never use. Chipped or mismatched dishes. Expired spices and pantry items. Cleaning supplies that are nearly empty. Items you're donating or selling — get them out of the kitchen entirely.

---

## Declutter tips for the kitchen specifically

Go shelf by shelf and ask "have I used this in the past year?" If not, it goes in a donate box or the trash. Spices older than 2–3 years have lost most of their flavor — smell them and be ruthless. Tupperware breeds in the dark; keep only containers that have matching lids. You don't need seven spatulas. Partial bottles of cleaning products aren't worth moving 2,400 miles. Perishable food, opened oils, and anything that could leak should not go on the truck.

---

## Packing tips for fragile kitchen items

Wrap plates individually in packing paper and stand them on edge in the box like records — they're stronger that way than stacked flat. Nest bowls with paper between each one. Stuff mugs and glasses with crumpled paper inside, then wrap the outside. Put heavy items (cast iron, stoneware) in small boxes so nobody hurts their back. Fill every gap in every box with paper or towels so nothing shifts. Mark "FRAGILE — KITCHEN" and an arrow for "this side up" on all sides.

Want me to do the next room, or move on to the calendar reminders or the moving-day one-pager?
